column1: # DRC waivers for drc.sh — known asap7-KLayout-port artifacts and checks the
# OpenROAD router cannot satisfy (deferred to the authoritative ASAP7 Calibre
# deck). The shipped KLayout deck is run UNMODIFIED; drc.sh classifies each
# violation as waived (listed here, with justification) or unwaived. drc.sh
# fails (exit 1) only on UNWAIVED violations — so a clean block is one with no
# *new/unexplained* DRC, and every suppression here is auditable.
# Format (tab-separated):  rule_id <TAB> class <TAB> justification
#   class ARTIFACT — the KLayout port mis-encodes the rule vs the official DRM
#                    (the geometry is DRM-clean; the check is wrong)
#   class DEFER    — real/plausible rule, but router-blind or PDK-internal
#                    geometry this flow cannot act on; Calibre signs it off
# See issue #39 for the DRM investigation behind these.
# rule_id

column3: DRM nominal M4 spacing is 24nm (M4.S.1); the real M4.S.5 is parallel-run-length>=44nm, NOT a spacing. laurentc2's port mis-encodes it as space(25nm), false-flagging the compliant 24nm grid on every short edge. asap7_drm_201207a.pdf 3.14.
DRM nominal M5 spacing is 24nm (M5.S.1); identical 25nm-spacing mis-encoding of a parallel-run-length rule as M4.S.5.

M1 width-dependent spacing (25nm when one edge >36nm). TritonRoute self-DRC=0 — the router does not model it; not fixable by re-hardening. Calibre signs off. (Deck also leaves this rule's category name blank.)
M1 corner-to-corner (euclidian) 20nm. Router does not model diagonal corner spacing; self-DRC=0. Defer to Calibre.
V1 corner-to-corner spacing w/ a 5nm M2 end-cap — exotic via-corner rule the router does not model. Defer to Calibre.
